daily.title: Daily Review: 2026-06-08

sections.Goal: Create the Day 1 launch operating system and prepare SEMrush-driven paid-search research.
sections.Completed:
- Confirmed product can ship in 14-21 days.
- Chose mature-brand positioning instead of Founder Batch framing.
- Chose $149 as the initial hardware price.
- Selected SEMrush as the first research API source.
- Started Launch OS planning and version control.
- Created the Launch OS local workspace, dashboard, data scripts, templates, and deployment scaffold.
- Deployed the first public Launch OS dashboard to `http://124.174.96.149:8798/`.
- Added a Volcengine security group rule for `tcp/8798` after confirming requests did not reach the ECS.
- Upgraded the public dashboard into a project cockpit with overview, daily review, decisions, operations, cost notes, SEMrush readiness, and next actions.
- Created local Codex Skill `focusfence-launch-os` so future sessions read Launch OS records before acting.
- Added SEMrush runbook and seed keyword preview script.
sections.Data Findings:
- SEMrush is expected to support paid-search competitor, ad copy, keyword, and landing-page research.
- Google Keyword Planner should be used later to validate final keyword volume, bid ranges, and forecasts.
sections.Mistakes Or Corrections:
- Earlier channel thinking over-weighted Meta and under-specified SEM demand-keyword strategy.
- Earlier brand framing over-emphasized Founder Batch/first production run; the current direction is mature product launch.

- Decide the first Google Search campaign structure from data.
- Add domain/HTTPS or decide whether port-based access is acceptable for internal launch work.
- Add `SEMRUSH_API_KEY` to `.env.local` and pull the first keyword data.
sections.Open Questions:
- Exact brand/domain to use publicly.
- Return window and customer support policy.
- US shipping method and cost.

decisions.title: Decision 001: Mature Product Positioning
decisions.decision: Use mature-brand product positioning. Do not lead with Founder Batch, first production run, or early-device framing.
evidence: The product can ship in 14-21 days.
The user wants cold-traffic paid conversion, not community crowdfunding.
AI + faith + wearable creates enough trust burden already; early-stage language can increase perceived risk.
decisions.reversalCriteria: Revisit if cold traffic shows low trust despite strong click intent, or if fulfillment constraints force a preorder/deposit model.

decisions.title: Decision 002: Initial Price $149
decisions.decision: Set the first public hardware price at $149.
evidence: Product visuals support a premium black-and-gold faith wearable.
The product includes hardware plus a companion software experience.
$149 keeps the product below mainstream premium wearable pricing while staying meaningfully above app-only subscriptions.
decisions.reversalCriteria: Revisit if high-intent Search traffic reaches checkout but fails to convert because of price or shipping trust concerns.

decisions.title: Decision 003: SEMrush First For Research
decisions.decision: Use SEMrush API as the first data source for paid-search strategy research.
evidence: SEMrush is better suited to competitor paid-search, ad copy, paid keyword, and landing-page discovery.
Google Keyword Planner is better as a final validation source for search volume, bid ranges, and forecasts.
Ahrefs is useful for organic/SERP/content research, but less directly aligned with the first SEM strategy question.
decisions.reversalCriteria: Revisit if SEMrush data lacks paid-search coverage for relevant Christian, Scripture, prayer, anxiety, anger, and stress keyword clusters.

decisions.title: Decision 004: Continuity Through Skill And Records
decisions.decision: Use both repository records and a local Codex Skill to preserve Launch OS continuity across sessions.
evidence: Chat history can be compacted or lost.
Repository files are versioned and auditable.
A Skill can force future sessions to read Launch OS records before acting.
decisions.reversalCriteria: Revisit if the Skill does not trigger reliably in future sessions or if another project-level instruction mechanism becomes more reliable.

operations.title: Operation: Launch OS Bootstrap
operations.summary: Created the first Launch OS project system, deployed it publicly, and committed the Day 1 implementation.
resources: Added a new systemd service named `launch-os`.
Added a zero-dependency Node static server on port `8798`.
Added one security group ingress rule for `tcp/8798` from `0.0.0.0/0`.
Did not change the existing DeepResponse service on port `8797`.
Did not create a new ECS server.
Did not install Docker on the ECS.
Did not commit cloud or API secrets.
operations.cost: No new server was created during this operation. The public dashboard currently runs on the already-existing postpaid Volcengine ECS instance `ecs.g4i.large` with a 5 Mbps EIP. The incremental Launch OS cost is expected to be negligible while it shares the existing instance, but the actual cloud bill must be verified in the Volcengine billing console because postpaid ECS, bandwidth, storage, and traffic are account-level charges.
verification: `npm run launch:verify` passed with 5 Launch OS tests.
